sources.entry: Claude Code PM by Ran Aroussi - Really comprehensive and feature-packed project-management workflow for Claude Code. Numerous specialized agents, slash-commands, and strong documentation.

summary.one_liner: CCPM is an Agent Skill that gives coding agents a spec-driven project-management workflow: PRDs become epics, epics become tasks, and tasks sync to GitHub issues for parallel execution.
summary.what_it_does: The skill guides an agent through brainstorming and writing a PRD, then parsing it into a technical epic with architecture decisions. The epic is broken into task files with acceptance criteria, effort estimates, and depends_on, parallel, and conflicts_with metadata. A sync step creates a GitHub epic issue with sub-issues, renames local task files to the issue numbers, and sets up a dedicated git worktree. Agents then analyze an issue for independent work streams and run them in parallel, committing with issue-referenced messages. Status, standup, search, and next/blocked reports are produced by bash scripts that read the local project files in .claude/. The README says it is harness-agnostic and follows the agentskills.io standard.
use_cases: Turn a feature idea into a PRD and technical epic
Break a large feature into parallelizable tasks for AI agents
Sync local project plans to GitHub issues and sub-issues
Run multiple agents on independent parts of one issue
Generate daily standup and blocked-task reports from project files
Keep traceable context for AI-assisted development across sessions
how_to_run: ln -s /path/to/ccpm/skill/ccpm .claude/skills/ccpm  (Claude Code, run in project root)
Authenticate the GitHub CLI with: gh auth login
Optionally install the sub-issue extension: gh extension install yahsan2/gh-sub-issue
Talk to your agent naturally, e.g. "I want to build X" or "standup"
notable: Project state lives in plain markdown files under .claude/, with GitHub Issues as the shared source of truth
Deterministic operations like status, standup, and search run as bash scripts without LLM token cost
Each epic gets its own git worktree so parallel agents work in isolation
Works across multiple agent harnesses that support the Agent Skills standard
Intentionally avoids the GitHub Projects API, relying on issues, labels, and milestones
caveats: Requires the git and gh CLI, authenticated, plus a GitHub repository
Parent-child sub-issue links need the separate gh-sub-issue extension; otherwise it falls back to task lists
Benchmark and productivity figures are self-reported in the README and not independently verified
The original v1 /pm:* slash-command system is only preserved on the v1 branch
